title: zone-aware-init-priority-and-jittered-backoff-values
author: Maya Patel
body: Motivation: private deployments running in multi-AZ and on-prem clusters were observing uneven init job placement, occasional head-of-line blocking when tenant bootstrap jobs became heavy, and fragile upgrade windows when all init jobs retried simultaneously. This PR adds a focused set of Helm values and template changes to make init orchestration zone-aware, priority-safe, and more resilient via jittered backoff and optional leader-election for cross-namespace coordination. Key user-visible changes: 1) values.init.priorityClassName: allow operators to pin init jobs to a provided PriorityClass so critical migrations run ahead of low-priority tenants; 2) values.init.zoneSpread.enabled and values.init.zoneSpread.constraints: basic affinity/nodeSelector helpers so customers in multi-AZ environments can prefer spreading boot jobs across zones to avoid resource churn in a single AZ; 3) values.init.backoff: tunable backoff.initialSeconds, multiplier, and jitterPercent to avoid synchronized retry storms during cluster upgrades; 4) values.init.leaderElection.enable (default false) and values.init.leaderElection.namespace to optionally use a namespaced ConfigMap lock for sequencing cross-namespace init waves in air-gapped environments where API-server watch latencies are variable; 5) transitional defaults and migration notes so existing installs are opt-in and safe for rolling upgrades. This PR also updates the terraform module reference docs to demonstrate how to pass these new values from top-level installs, and adds unit tests for the Helm templates plus a small e2e job that simulates staggered init waves. Backwards compatibility: all fields are opt-in with sensible defaults; existing installs will continue to use previous behavior unless values are provided. See Linear tickets ENG-4821 and ENG-4990 for the broader rollout plan and gating alongside the runtime batching feature. Checklist: - [x] Helm values schema additions and comments - [x] Template changes for init Job/cronjob - [x] Add priorityClassName to init Job spec - [x] Add optional nodeAffinity/zone spread helpers - [x] Implement jittered backoff calculation in template helpers - [x] Add leader-election ConfigMap lock templating and RBAC snippets - [x] Unit tests for template rendering (helm unittest) - [x] Terraform docs example updated - [x] Manual QA: staged upgrade on dev cluster with 3 zones - [x] Release notes entry drafted

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can we ensure the default backoff.jitterPercent is conservative (15%)? Observed larger jitter can postpone critical migrations during recovery. Author reply: Set default to 15% in values.schema.json and added note in docs about tradeoffs.

Priya Raman: Leader election across namespaces is tricky for airgapped clusters because the operator's service account may not have cluster-scoped permissions. Suggest we make it explicit that leaderElection default is false and include RBAC snippets. Author reply: Done — added namespaced ConfigMap lock and RBAC via charts/private-installer/templates/rbac-init.yaml; leaderElection.enable defaults to false.

Liam O'Connor: Template helper complexity looks fine but add a unit test that asserts backoff seconds never exceed a configured cap. Author reply: Added a helm-unittest case that validates maxBackoffSeconds <= 3600 when multiplier and initialSeconds are high.

Security review (automated): noted that the leader lock uses ConfigMap writes; ensure audit logging and KMS keys are not referenced here. Author reply: This PR keeps leader lock ConfigMap scoped and documents that audit logging is provided by cluster logging — no secrets written.
QA (manual): Verified staged upgrade on dev cluster across 3 AZs; init jobs spread across AZs when zoneSpread.enabled=true; observed expected reduction in retry storms after jitter enabled.
Merge-resolver bot: lint fixes applied to templates via a small follow-up commit to address Helm lint warning about missing metadata. Author reply: incorporated fixes and re-ran unit tests.
release_notes: Add opt-in init orchestration values: init.priorityClassName, init.zoneSpread, init.backoff (initialSeconds, multiplier, jitterPercent), and init.leaderElection (namespaced lock). These improve init job placement and resilience during upgrades. Defaults preserve existing behavior.
notes_for_ops: If you operate multi-AZ clusters and see init job contention during upgrades, consider enabling init.zoneSpread and a non-default priorityClassName for critical tenant migrations. On air-gapped installs, enable init.leaderElection with a namespace-scoped lock and ensure RBAC is applied. When backoff.jitterPercent is increased, monitor upgrade window length and adjust multiplier accordingly.
